author: Claude Opus 5.5 (engineering lead) with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (cand-a v3 implementation agent)
summary: Hexagonal-prism tumbler, version 3: one rigid hexagonal body (circumradius 25.5 mm) that rolls over its hexagon edges, driven by an internal lift ring with one lobe (geared from a 6 mm gearmotor, 304 internal-gear band in a PA12 carrier); axial couplers on the two end faces: a machined 304 hex peg on the head (6.5 mm engagement), and a tail receiver with roll-in channel, yaw turntable, a 304 hex-in-hex roll lock and a motor-driven over-centre four-bar keeper (third gearmotor, no SMA, no spring). BLE only, no power transfer.

components.description: yaw turntable puck (PA12), cylinder dia 7.6 mm (r 3.8), axis z through (x 0, y -8.2), z -3.5 to 6.9 mm. components.description: keeper drive four-bar (304, machined ISO 2768-1 class f): crank r 2.0 on the M3 axis (x 11.25, z 10.25), crank 0.8 x 3 x 4 = 9.6 mm3 at y -9.2 to -8.4; link 10.216 mm long (equal to the pivot-to-crank-axis distance D = 10.2159 mm), 0.8 x 1.5 x 10.216 = 12.26 mm3; rocker (bell crank) pivot at (x 1.5, z 13.3), OFF the yaw axis, link-side arm b = 3.0 and output arm a = 4.5 at -46 deg from the link-side arm, 0.8 x 1.5 x (3.0 + 4.5 + 1.25 boss allowance) = 10.50 mm3 (upper branch: rocker pin above the pivot); dia 0.8 x 18 push rod on the yaw axis (x 0) through the hollow yaw shaft = 9.05 mm3, driven from the output pin through a pin-in-slot; two hard stops 1 x 1 x 2 = 4 mm3; four pins 7.54 mm3 (volume as budgeted by the lead; four dia 0.8 x 3 pins would be 6.03 mm3, an upper bound). Dead centres at crank-link collinear positions: extended |B-C| = L + r, folded L - r. Stops are 10 deg past each dead centre; the crank travels 197.5 deg between them and the rocker swings 82.7 deg. Rod stroke between the stops 5.58 mm (needs 5.2). At either stop the link line passes on the stop side of the crank axis (offsets 0.407 mm at the extended stop, 0.283 mm at the folded stop), so tongue loads push the crank into its stop (no power, no spring). assembly_access.statement: Walls and end plates are separate PA12 parts joined by two PA12 axial posts (from y -6.9 to the head end plate; the tail end plate is joined through the tail cap halves) and four M1.6 screws (screw positions are a lumped stand-in). Each wall half (head and tail) is a separate part so the lift ring (PA12 carrier segments with pressed-in 304 gear band segments) can be dropped into the girdle slot between them. The cell, controller and boards load as a stack along the axis with one end plate removed; the head peg installs from the head end plate and the tail receiver cap halves, yaw puck (with the pressed-in 304 cup insert) and keeper (with its jaw) install from the tail end. The keeper push rod runs inside the hollow yaw shaft, and the crank and link lie in the M3 shaft zone. No assembly sequence has been verified, and the gear train, yaw worm, keeper four-bar routing and the press fits of the gear band and the cup insert are not shown to be assemblable.

coupler_sites.mount: datum on the head peg axis where a neighbour's tail face sits when docked (gap g = 8 mm from the head end face at y = 14 mm, 5 mm peg engagement)
tail receiver on end plate b (tail face)

retention.mechanism: The head peg's annular groove (dia 3.0 x 1.4 wide, groove centre at A-frame y 27.1 = 5.1 mm inside the neighbour's face at y 22; engagement depth 6.5 mm, peg tip y 28.5) is closed by a 1.0 mm 304 keeper tongue (B frame y -9.4 to -8.4 in the groove y -9.6 to -8.2). The tongue is moved by a motor-driven over-centre four-bar: crank r 2.0 on the M3 axis (x 11.25, z 10.25), link 10.216 mm, rocker (bell crank) with its pivot at (x 1.5, z 13.3) off the yaw axis (link-side arm 3.0, output arm 4.5), and a dia 0.8 push rod on the yaw axis driven through a pin-in-slot. Two stable states, both geometric: CLOSED = crank 10 deg past the folded dead centre against a hard stop, OPEN = crank 10 deg past the extended dead centre against a second stop (the crank travels 197.5 deg between them, the rocker 82.7 deg, the rod 5.58 mm for 5.2 mm needed). At either stop the link line passes on the stop side of the crank axis (by 0.283 mm at the closed stop and 0.407 mm at the open stop), so any load on the tongue pushes the crank into its stop; no power and no spring hold either state. With ISO 2768-1 class f tolerances on all the four-bar dimensions (r, b, pivot and crank positions +-0.05, link +-0.1, stop +-0.05) the worst-case margin past the dead centre stays at least 6 deg. Tension path: peg groove shoulder, tongue, 1.0 mm PA12 front wall of the puck (puck front face y -12.0, tongue at y -9.4 to -8.4 behind a jaw and cup zone y -11.0 to -9.6), thrust on the inner face of end plate b through an annulus r 2.8 to 3.8 (20.7 mm2); the puck runs as a journal in a dia 8.8 bore of the cap halves (length 3.5 mm). Roll lock: when closed the peg hex section (4.0 mm across flats) is fully enclosed over 1.4 mm by the 304 cup insert (lower half-hex, pressed into the puck) and the upper half-hex jaw on the keeper slider, both 4.10 mm across flats (0.05 mm clearance per side, free roll +-2.58 deg); torsion passes from the peg flats to the insert and jaw and from the puck to the body through the hollow 304 yaw shaft. Nothing is powered to hold.

release.means: The unit's own keeper motor M3 (Precision Microdrives 206-109 via driver-2) drives the crank back over the dead centres: it turns the crank 197 deg from the closed stop to the open stop, and the four-bar retracts the tongue by 5.58 mm (5.2 mm needed: closed lower edge z -1.0, open z >= 4.2). The open state is held geometrically and unpowered by the second stop. Release torque: with tongue friction at the full design tension (steel on steel, mu bound 1.0, provisional, no coefficient cited) the design tension is 4 mu W = 1.642 N for the declared 41.849 g mass, so the tongue friction force is 1.642 N and the peak crank torque over the stroke is 1.642 N x 3.025 mm = 4.97 mN m (the largest tongue-to-crank lever over the stroke) against M3 rated 3 mN m (0.60x of the requirement) and stall 9 mN m (1.81x). Release under the full mu = 1 bound tension therefore needs more than the rated M3 torque; rated torque covers tongue friction up to 0.99 N (60% of the bound). At zero tension only the friction of the mechanism acts (unquantified). Release is specified at low chain tension: the controller relaxes the tension first (chain yaw 0, no drag). Docking sequence: open keeper (M3), roll in, IMU detects landing, close keeper (M3). It acts only on this unit's own receiver and needs no help from the neighbour, which can also roll away about the same edge. Crank stop wear, M3 heat and cycle life are UNRESOLVED.

alignment.description: Roll-in channel: two circular-arc slots in the tail cap halves, radius 25.5 mm, centred on the two bottom vertices, from the mid-height vertices to the face centre, 5.8 mm wide, 7.0 mm deep from the tail face, 45 deg x 1.5 mm flared mouths (peg engagement 6.5 mm).
alignment.justification: When unit B rolls one step about its leading bottom edge, a neighbour's peg lying on the common axis moves in B's frame along exactly this arc, keeps its direction (parallel to y) and turns 60 deg about its own axis (hex symmetry), so B can roll into a docked pose using its own lift drive and gravity. Slot width 5.8 mm (4.619 + 2 x 0.59, no functional PA12 clearance below 0.6 mm in the design rule, no PA12 wall below 1.0 mm) against the 4.619 mm across-corner peg gives 0.59 mm per side nominal. SLS accuracy +-0.3% with a lower limit of +-0.3 mm (Materialise PA12 SLS, https://www.materialise.com/en/industrial/3d-printing-materials/pa12-sls) gives a minimum width 5.5 mm and a minimum clearance 0.44 mm per side. Windows (nominal, minimum with SLS): lateral at the mouth +-(0.59+1.5) = +-2.09 mm (min +-1.94); height +-0.59 mm (min +-0.44); heading +-atan(0.59/5) = +-6.7 deg (min +-5.0); roll any multiple of 60 deg; final lateral seating by the tongue V-notch +-1.45 mm; axial +-0.5 mm (lash of the joint: groove play +-0.2 plus puck-slot play +-0.3; with ISO f and SLS tolerances +-0.3 to +-0.7). THERE IS NO AXIAL OR HEADING PRE-ALIGNMENT MEANS other than these windows: the unit has no steering and no axial motion, so docking requires a common lane (axial error and heading inside the windows) as a precondition, not as a capability. The pre-alignment covers only the in-plane roll-in. After docking the relative roll is 0: B rolls from face F1 (or F5) onto F0 and A rests on F0, and the 60 deg that the peg turns relative to B during entry is absorbed by the hex symmetry (the roll lock then has +-2.6 deg of free roll). These are nominal geometric estimates; the capture window is not claimed (CPL-006) and is to be measured by sweeps. No magnet and no cone.

alignment.description: Tongue V-notch seating: the keeper tongue has a V-notch (3.1 mm for the 3.0 mm groove, 6.0 mm mouth, 30 deg half-angle) and a 30 deg half-angle wedge lead-in (0.3 mm each side, tip face 0.4 mm thick) that centre the peg in the half-hex cup as the crank closes.
alignment.justification: The notch mouth (6.0 - 3.1)/2 = +-1.45 mm laterally pulls the peg into the cup as the tongue closes. Axial capture is +-0.5 mm (groove play +-0.2 plus the 0.3 mm lead-in). The tongue is driven by M3 through the four-bar, not by a spring: the closing force at the tongue is at least rated 3 mN m / 3.03 mm = 0.99 N over the whole stroke (stall 2.97 N) against the other unit's head-end friction mu W/2 = 0.205 N at mu = 1 for the declared 41.849 g mass, a ratio of 4.8 (rated), UNRESOLVED dynamically; the wedge factor and tongue flank friction are not applied. Machined 304 tongue and groove (ISO 2768-1 class f, https://amesweb.info/fits-tolerances/iso-2768-linear-dimensions-tolerances.aspx): notch 3.1 mm against groove 3.0 mm leaves 0.05 mm per side nominal, from 0 to 0.1 mm over the +-0.05 mm tolerances. Passive geometry and a gearmotor.

alignment.description: Hex peg in half-hex cup with 0.5 x 45 deg tip chamfer on the peg.
alignment.justification: The hexagonal peg (4.0 mm across flats) has six equivalent roll positions every 60 deg and is guided into the lower half-hex cup of the 304 cup insert (4.10 mm across flats, 0.05 mm clearance per side, opening upward) by its 0.5 mm chamfer; the upper half-hex jaw on the keeper closes the hex over 1.4 mm. The flats carry torsion after a free roll of +-2.58 deg. Contact forces at the lash limit are 2.46 N (one idle neighbour tipped, 5.23 mN m) and 4.92 N (10.47 mN m) per contact on 304 flats; the cam-out force along the tongue axis is at most 4.92 N and is carried by the over-centre stop, not a spring. No attractive force acts: a unit that is not driven does not self-dock.

limitations: Roll-in docking was checked on paper only; the dynamics (impact, whether the ring-driven roll lands inside the windows) and the capture window are UNRESOLVED and belong to later gates. There is no axial or heading pre-alignment means; docking requires a common lane.
No steering or axial locomotion is provided: the body rolls only perpendicular to its axis.

Yaw bending works only while the chain rests on a face with a vertical yaw axis. The worm self-locks only if the worm/sector friction coefficient is at least 0.125 (UNRESOLVED), so a bend angle is treated as actively maintained. Yaw torque margin at table mu = 1 is 0.96 at rated motor torque for the declared 41.849 g mass (below 1): bending at rated torque holds only for table mu <= about 0.96, which is the bound operating envelope for bending (stall torque covers mu 1 with a ratio 2.88).

Release under the full mu = 1 design tension needs more than the rated M3 torque (rated 0.60x of the requirement, stall 1.81x); release is specified at low tension. Crank stop wear, tongue friction coefficient (mu bound 1.0 is provisional, not cited) and M3 heat and cycle life are UNRESOLVED. M3 adds 1.2 g and 851 mW peak.

Many masses are upper bounds from solid volumes (walls, end plates, caps, puck, peg, lobe, gear band); the placement of the screws and the harness is a lumped stand-in; the peg root box, keeper and keeper-linkage boxes (the crank lies in the M3 shaft zone, the rod inside the hollow yaw shaft), the puck bore inside the cap boxes and the meshing gears are box approximations. Four keeper pins are budgeted at 7.54 mm3, an upper bound; the jaw block (7.0 x 1.4 x 3.05) and the cup insert block are solid upper bounds; the push rod meets the rocker output pin through a pin-in-slot (slot length not declared, the pin moves 2.4 mm in x); the keeper-linkage box is higher (z to 17.3) than first requested because the 5.6 mm output pin travel cannot fit 4.8 mm. Hertz contact stress at the peg corners on the 304 flats with an assumed 0.1 mm edge radius exceeds the first-yield rule of thumb (local indentation expected).

Gear teeth are integer: ring 133 T pitch r 19.95 (304 band, machined) and pinion 14 T pitch r 2.1 (module 0.3, centre distance 17.85); spurs 41 T and 16 T at module 0.2 (centre distance 5.70); yaw worm 1 start into 27 teeth per turn at module 0.3. Tooth strength, backlash, profile and contact ratio are not assessed. No PA12 gear teeth remain.

Tolerances: SLS PA12 accuracy is cited from Materialise (https://www.materialise.com/en/industrial/3d-printing-materials/pa12-sls) as +-0.3% with a lower limit of +-0.3 mm and minimum wall 1 mm; machined 304 parts are specified ISO 2768-1 class f (https://amesweb.info/fits-tolerances/iso-2768-linear-dimensions-tolerances.aspx), +-0.05 mm for 0.5 to 6 mm and +-0.1 mm for 6 to 30 mm. Materialise is a service-provider page, not EOS PA 2200 material data; whether a given printer reaches these values is not shown. PA12 strength is not assessed beyond the coupler checks; heat is not assessed.

The Precision Microdrives 206-109 datasheet is headed as a sampling/target specification; the three motors run from 3.7 V by PWM limited to 3.0 V effective, a control constraint. The datasheet gives no radial shaft load rating, which the crank link force loads.

The QT Py regulator is rated 600 mA peak; the 2220 mW term is a bound; later board revisions may use a different regulator. The board has no LiPo charger, and regulator dropout limits use near the end of charge.

Vendor product pages (Grepow, Adafruit, Pololu, Materialise, amesweb) are classed datasheet because the schema allows only datasheet or publication. Cited values were read on 2026-11-06 and are checked by sampling at the gate record.
A2 screws are costed at 304 density (assumption).
Only two axial couplers are declared; no lateral side-face couplers, no branching or lattices. No through-coupler data or power contacts; power transfer is not provided.
